question: to the Commission Geadis Geadi (ECR) Subject:

With this question I would like to condemn the recent statements by Turkish Interior Minister Mustafa Çiftçi, who expressed the wish to one day become ‘Jerusalem’s Governor’ and suggested that the city would eventually return to Ottoman rule. He further declared that, just as Türkiye witnessed the so-called ‘liberation’ of Damascus, Aleppo and Nagorno-Karabakh, it may also witness the ‘liberation of Jerusalem’.1 These remarks form part of a broader pattern of revisionist and neo-Ottoman rhetoric emanating from senior Turkish officials, challenging the sovereignty and territorial integrity of neighbouring states and contributing to instability across the Eastern Mediterranean and the Middle East. Such statements are particularly alarming given Türkiye’s continued military occupation of part of the Republic of Cyprus and its persistent threats against the sovereign rights of EU Member States. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission condemn these statements by the Turkish Minister of the Interior?

Given that Türkiye continues to receive substantial EU financial assistance, does the Commission intend to examine whether repeated revisionist claims and threats to the sovereignty of third states should have consequences for EU funding and political engagement with Türkiye?
https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/turkish-interior-minister-hopes-for-liberation-of-jerusalem/news
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.8.2026) The EU has stated repeatedly its deep concern about such statements, expressing its expectation by Türkiye to de-escalate tensions in the interest of regional stability in the Eastern Mediterranean1. In particular, the Commission has underlined in the 2025 enlargement report on Türkiye that the latter is expected to make an unequivocal commitment to good neighbourly relations, international agreements and the peaceful settlement of disputes having recourse, if necessary, to the International Court of Justice2.
